items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 135:1
items.html: The ten Sefirot of direct light are the four phases of the expansion of the light of Ein Sof. The ten Sefirot of reflected light are the lights that are returned and rejected from Malchut, as above in Item 119. And the ten Sefirot whose level is equal are the ten Sefirot of direct light that are clothed in ten Sefirot of reflected light out of a single coupling by striking, as above in Item 194. And the ten Sefirot that stand one above the other are those that emerge from four couplings by striking that are made in Malchut in the way of her refining, that is, at the time of her ascent from the Tabur to the Peh, as above in Item 142. And the ten Sefirot that stand one below the other emerge from five couplings by striking, after Malchut comes each time to the Peh and receives a new coarseness there, as above in Item 168. And the ten Sefirot of the Rosh are from Malchut upward, before she comes into a state of clothing, as above in Item 141. And the ten Sefirot of the Toch are from Malchut downward, as above in Item 142. And the ten Sefirot of the Sof are reflected light without direct light, since they are from Malchut downward after she has come into the clothing of the lights; and they are therefore the ones that conclude the Partzuf, as above in Item 143. And the five phases in the vessel of Malchut are from the records from Ein Sof that remained in Malchut after the restriction, as above in Item 119. And the four phases of roots of vessels in potential are of the phases of the spark of the Creator, as above in Item 210. And the four phases of roots of vessels in actuality are of the phases of the spark of the created being, as above in Item 210.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 135:2
items.html: And know that in the matter of the ten Sefirot that stand one above the other, which are the particular ten Sefirot in every Partzuf, there are no vessels there for Haya and Yechida, because these ten Sefirot emerge by means of a coupling by striking in the way of the refining of Malchut, as above (in Item 95 and Item 142). And since the coarseness of phase one is very faint, a coupling by striking does not operate in her to such a degree, for she does not raise reflected light in a measure sufficient for the clothing of the direct light to the measure that its above-downward aspect should become a vessel. And it goes without saying that no coupling by striking operates at the time when she has been refined entirely, as in the phase of Keter. Therefore there are only three vessels there, which are from phase two, phase three and phase four; but from the phase of Keter and from phase one there are no vessels there, and the lights Haya and Yechida must be clothed in the internality of the Neshama, that is, in the light of Bina (as above in Item 163).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 135:3
items.html: And you must remember here to discern between the phase of drawing and the phase of reception that are present in every Sefira (as above in Item 157 and Item 158). And it turns out accordingly that what we said here, that there are no vessels for the light of Yechida and the light of Haya, refers only to a vessel of reception; but a vessel of drawing she does have, for the vessel of drawing of the light of Haya is phase three, and the vessel of drawing of the light of Yechida is phase four — and these phases are present in completeness in the Partzufim of AK. Therefore we said here that the lights Haya and Yechida do exist, only that they are clothed in the Neshama.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 135:4
items.html: However, from the time of the association of the quality of mercy with judgement onward, that is, from BON of AK onward (as above in Item 176) — when phase three and phase four were lacking from the Partzufim and became surrounding ones, which are called garment and hall — the vessels of drawing for Haya and Yechida in all the Partzufim were found to be lacking as well. It turns out that the lights of Haya and Yechida too are not in the Partzuf, for there is no phase four here to draw the light of Yechida, and there is no phase three here to draw the light of Haya. And remember this. And know that this matter of the absence of ZON that has been mentioned is only in relation to AK; but in relation to themselves, they certainly have complete ten Sefirot, as is written in their place.
